metaDescription: Convert frequency to wavelength and get half-wave dipole, quarter-wave and full-wave antenna lengths with a velocity factor, in metres, feet and inches.
intro: Cut an antenna to length for a radio band from its frequency.
why:
Wavelength is the speed of light divided by frequency. The page lists free-space wavelength and, with your velocity factor (0.95 for bare wire, around 0.66 for coax), the full, half, quarter and 5/8 wave lengths in metres, feet and inches, plus the common 468/f(MHz) feet shortcut for a half-wave dipole.

Real antennas need trimming for height, nearby objects and conductor thickness; use an antenna analyser or SWR meter to tune.

No data is sent anywhere: the work happens in your browser, so you can use it offline once the page has loaded.
howTo: Cut slightly long and trim for the lowest SWR.

faq.a: The speed of the signal in the conductor relative to light; it shortens the physical length.
An empirical constant for a half-wave dipole that includes the end effect.

faq.q: Does it design the matching network?

faq.a: No. Everything is processed in your browser, and the page makes no network requests with your input.
